correspondence.excerpt: A Context Map is not a directory tree, dependency scan, import graph, ontology relation set, runtime topology, authority transfer, or evidence that two contexts agree.
A map records dependent classifications through relations; it does not add redundant canonical axes to endpoint contexts.
Generated reverse membership is disposable lookup state and cannot override the map that generated it.

This candidate revises Context Map meaning to make the map the sole canonical owner of endpoint membership and directional relations. It does not supersede v1, admit this version, revise an artifact type or map instance, generate a live reverse index, authorize migration, or establish a stable release.
Canonical endpoint membership and directional semantic or integration relationships between exact Bounded Context versions.

Directory trees, import graphs, runtime topology, and authority transfer.
Canonical backreferences or duplicated map-membership axes on endpoint Bounded Contexts.
contexts/maps/governance-ontology-lifecycle/v2/map.json would own both exact v2 endpoint references and the Governance-to-Ontology-Lifecycle direction.
A generated index may answer which maps mention cal.context.ontology-lifecycle/v2 without becoming a second authority.

A successor Governance-to-Ontology-Lifecycle map can name the admitted v2 contexts directly without forcing those contexts to name that map. The reverse lookup belongs in a generated index, which removes the version cycle found after CTX05.

The one authoritative record of which exact bounded-context versions participate in a relationship and how information moves between them. Contexts do not copy that membership back into themselves.
Both endpoint identities and versions are explicit in the map.
Direction and authority limits cannot be inferred from imports.
One mapping pattern is selected by its owners, not by this generic definition.
An endpoint backreference cannot establish, amend, or revoke map membership.
ContextMap = (id, version, context_refs, relationships, owner_refs, lifecycle, evidence_refs, drift_route)
Relationship = (source_context_version, target_context_version, direction, relationship_kind, contract_refs, translation_refs, information_boundary, authority_boundary, owners)
CanonicalOwner(context_refs,relationships) = ContextMap
ReverseMembershipIndex(c) = {m.id | c in m.context_refs}
; Proximity does not imply Relationship.
A Context Map is a versioned, owner-approved set of exact Bounded Context endpoints and typed directional relationships between them.
The Context Map is the sole canonical owner of its endpoint membership and relationships.
Each relationship declares source and target roles, integration or translation contracts, information and authority limits, owners, evidence, drift handling, and change coordination.
Endpoint contexts do not canonically backreference the map; reverse membership is generated by indexing canonical Context Maps.
The complete canonical endpoint set owned by one exact Context Map version.
context_refs
A generated lookup over admitted Context Maps for exact context version c.
ReverseMembershipIndex(c)
Every relationship has two exact endpoints, direction, kind, owners, and boundaries.
Every relationship endpoint occurs in the same map's context_refs.
No endpoint context is required to carry context_map_refs or an equivalent canonical backreference.
A reverse membership projection can be deleted and deterministically rebuilt from the admitted map registry.
